status_reason: MIR-ATR is a sound method for a solvent-based reactor liquid, but no supplied source shows a mid-infrared fiber link of 150 m or a loss figure for one, so the fibre choice and expected loss cannot be answered from the material provided.

premise_checks.premise: A mid-infrared fiber can carry the signal 150 m from reactor to analyser house.
premise_checks.explanation: Long cables (100-300 m) are stated only for low-OH silica fibers, which do not transmit mid-IR; the MIR fiber and hollow-waveguide examples in the sources are 1-2 m laboratory lengths, and no source states an achievable MIR link length or its loss.

requirements_stated: Follow a reaction in a solvent-based batch reactor with a mid-infrared ATR probe.
Spectrometer must stay in the analyser house about 150 m from the reactor for safety reasons.
Customer asks which fiber would carry the mid-infrared signal that far and what signal loss to expect.
key_unknowns: Whether a 150 m mid-infrared fiber link is technically achievable; no source states an MIR link length.
The mid-infrared spectral range the reaction monitoring needs, which decides between CIR, PIR fibers or hollow waveguides.
Target species, concentration ranges and solvent composition, which decide the method and calibration.
Process temperature and pressure at the probe.

clarification_questions.question: Which mid-infrared wavelength range does the reaction monitoring actually need (e.g. fingerprint bands around 6-10 um, or C-H/O-H regions nearer 3-4 um)?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The fiber family (CIR to 6.5 um, PIR to 17 um, hollow waveguide to 18 um) and its achievable length depend on the required range.

clarification_questions.question: Is the 150 m distance fixed, or could the spectrometer be placed closer to the reactor (e.g. at the reactor wall with only the data link remote)?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: A shorter optical link, or a fibre-coupled sensing head with remote electronics, changes the whole installation concept.

clarification_questions.question: Which species and concentration ranges must be followed, in which solvent, and at what process temperature and pressure?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: This decides whether MIR-ATR can see the targets, which crystal and probe design fit, and what calibration is needed.

clarification_questions.question: What measurement response time does the reaction monitoring require?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Acquisition speed influences the spectrometer and probe choice and any later multi-method synchronisation.

recommendations.rationale: MIR-ATR fiber probes are described for in-line liquid analysis without sampling, and MIR spectra give well-defined, selective bands for reaction components. It stays the first method to test, but only together with a fibre-link feasibility check, because no supplied source demonstrates a 150 m mid-infrared fiber link.
recommendations.conditions: Proceed only if a fibre (CIR, PIR or hollow waveguide) for the required spectral range can be sourced and tested at the required length with acceptable signal loss.

recommendations.rationale: Raman probes use silica fibers, for which robust 100-300 m cables are explicitly stated, so the 150 m distance is not a blocker; Raman also tolerates water and gives complementary bands. It is the benchmark against which the MIR-ATR option must prove itself given the link uncertainty.
recommendations.conditions: Check fluorescence background of the solvent and reaction mixture on real samples before relying on it.

measurement_concept.probe_and_geometry: Immersion MIR-ATR fiber probe (e.g. diamond or ZrO2 ATR tip) in the reactor liquid for M1; Raman immersion probe for M2.
measurement_concept.location: Probe tip in the batch reactor; spectrometer in the analyser house about 150 m away.
measurement_concept.fiber_link: M1 requires a mid-infrared fiber (CIR, PIR or hollow waveguide per the required range); no source states an achievable length or loss for such a link at 150 m, so this must be tested. M2 uses low-OH silica fiber, for which 100-300 m cables are stated.

steps.step: Collect representative reaction-mixture samples across the expected conversion range (start, mid, end points) in the actual solvent.
steps.purpose: Cover the chemical variation the model must handle.

steps.step: Record independent reference concentrations for each sample with a laboratory method (e.g. off-line FTIR, GC or HPLC as agreed with the customer).
steps.purpose: Provide the reference data for calibration and validation.

steps.step: On the bench, measure the samples with a short (lab-length) MIR-ATR fiber probe and, in parallel, a Raman probe; identify which bands track the reaction.
steps.purpose: Test each single method on its own before any combination or long-link commitment.

steps.step: Test candidate mid-infrared fibers (CIR, PIR, hollow waveguide) for the required wavelength range at increasing lengths up to the installed length, measuring throughput against the bench baseline.
steps.purpose: Establish whether the 150 m link delivers usable signal; this is the deciding experiment for M1.

steps.step: Build and validate the calibration on held-out batches, and apply the customer's go/no-go criteria (e.g. acceptable prediction error and signal-to-noise at the analyser house) before specifying the in-line installation.
steps.purpose: Confirm the chosen method meets the customer's performance requirements.

feasibility_plan.decision_basis: Customer-defined go/no-go criteria: minimum acceptable signal throughput at 150 m for the MIR link, and a maximum prediction error for the reaction species, both to be set by the customer.

chemometrics_note: Quantitative reaction following will need a calibration model built on representative samples with independent reference values, validated on held-out batches; the calibration is specific to this solvent matrix.
realtime_tracking_note: In-line, time-resolved tracking of the batch reaction is the goal; acquisition conditions should be chosen so the measurement rate matches the reaction kinetics.
future_direction: If the MIR link proves infeasible at 150 m, a fibre-coupled sensing head near the reactor with remote data communication, or a compact LED/sensor approach, could be evaluated later.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If no mid-infrared fiber can deliver acceptable signal at 150 m for the required spectral range, the choice moves to O1 (Raman over silica fiber) or to relocating the spectrometer closer to the reactor. The required wavelength range and whether the distance is fixed are the deciding answers.
proposal.next_step: Run the bench feasibility trial: measure representative reaction samples with a short MIR-ATR probe and test candidate MIR fibers at increasing lengths toward 150 m, with Raman as the comparison method.

brief_answer: MIR-ATR is a sensible method for your reactor liquid, but the supplied material does not show any mid-infrared fiber working at 150 m: long-reach cables are only stated for silica fibers, which do not transmit mid-IR, and MIR fibers appear only as 1-2 m lab samples. So neither the fiber choice nor a loss figure can be given yet. Test MIR-ATR with a fibre-link feasibility trial (CIR, PIR or hollow waveguide, depending on your required wavelength range), with Raman over silica fiber as the comparison option.
